intro: Riyadh rewards visitors who look past the highways to its museums, souqs and desert edge. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Riyadh Metro has six lines, running about 06:00 to midnight; a 2-hour ticket is SR 4.
Metro day passes cost about SR 20 for 3 days, SR 40 for 7 and SR 140 for 30; tickets include Riyadh Bus rides.
Riyadh Bus is the main city bus network; fares start around SR 4.
Taxis are plentiful; metered trips in town usually cost under SR 30.
Uber and Careem work well; many locals negotiate flat fares of SR 10-15 for short hops.
Driving is the local norm; walking is hard in the north but easy in Al-Bathaa's alleys.

stays.why: Central business district. Walkable to Kingdom Centre, cafés and the metro; easy taxis to most sights.
New financial district with modern hotels and metro links; quiet at night, good for business trips.
Old, budget-friendly heart near Souq Al-Thumairi and Masmak Fort; lively alleys, basic hotels.
Green, calm and embassies; upscale hotels and Wadi Hanifah walks nearby, but you need a car or taxi.

food: Try Saudi staples: kabsa (spiced rice with lamb or chicken), jareesh and kleija sweets.
Al-Bathaa and the old souq area have cheap shawarma, falafel and Indian cafeterias, often under SR 25 a meal.
For a splurge, book a modern Saudi or Levantine restaurant in Olaya or the Diplomatic Quarter; reserve on weekends.
Coffee culture is big: local roasteries serve Arabic coffee (qahwa) with dates; try them at a specialty café.
Alcohol is not sold anywhere. Many restaurants close briefly at prayer times; check opening hours on the day.
more_time: Add a Diriyah evening: the At-Turaif UNESCO site and nearby Bujairi Terrace restaurants are a highlight; check tickets on the day.
Edge of the World: a dramatic cliff viewpoint about 90 minutes' drive out; go with a tour or 4x4, not a normal sedan.
Swap a mall afternoon for Wadi Hanifah or Wadi Namar for a walk and picnic in cooler months.
